name: Columbia River (Hanford Reach)
gaugeName: Columbia River below Priest Rapids Dam
blurb: The last free-flowing, non-tidal stretch of the U.S. Columbia — White Bluffs, Hanford's reactors, salmon and eagles.

sections.notes: Huge river with strong, swirling current and wind-driven waves. Coyote Rapids (Class II) can be avoided. The Hanford Site is closed: you may not get out of your boat and enter the reservation. Flows swing up to 10 ft quickly with Priest Rapids Dam operations. NPS lists ~19 mi; USFWS lists 18 mi. Discover Pass required to park at Vernita Bridge (WDFW-managed, per NPS). No camping at Vernita (WDFW).

putInAccess.operator: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
putInAccess.sourceName: WDFW Facilities GIS, Boat Ramp layer (feature 25, unimproved; comment 'Location confirmed by R Finger, April 2025')
putInAccess.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is WDFW's own field-confirmed boat-ramp feature, not the site/staging point v1 used. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/vernita25.png) puts it on a gravel opening a few metres from the Columbia on the north shore, about 0.6 mi west (upstream) of Vernita Bridge, consistent with NPS's 'north shore just west of the bridge'. WDFW's second ramp feature (38, 'Location assigned', 46.643980, -119.734184) is in vegetation ~40 m from the water by the bridge and was not used. Legal access: WDFW Vernita Bridge page (https://wdfw.wa.gov/places-to-go/water-access-sites/vernita-bridge-1047) lists 2 unimproved ramps, open year-round; WaterAccessSites layer (https://geodataservices.wdfw.wa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/WP_RealEstate/WaterAccessSites/FeatureServer/1) shows WDFW-managed, no closure. Discover Pass or WDFW Vehicle Access Pass required.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~62 on the flowline), the ramp is on the north shore, left of the NHD centreline. Matches imagery and NPS.

takeOutAccess.operator: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Hanford Reach National Monument)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: USFWS Facilities/Property points (public view), 'White Bluffs Boat Ramp' (ObjectID 1215, asset 10004685, Public_Use 'Public Use', status Valid)
takeOutAccess.note: Batch 2. Coordinate is USFWS's own asset point for the ramp, separate from its 'White Bluffs Boat Ramp Parking' point (46.675380, -119.453112). Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch2/whitebluffs.png) puts it on the concrete ramp a few metres from the water's edge (the v1/OSM slipway point is ~11 m away). Legal access: USFWS Hanford Reach pages (https://www.fws.gov/national-monument/hanford-reach and .../visit-us/activities/boating---motorized) describe the concrete two-lane White Bluffs Boat Launch on the Wahluke Unit. It is CLOSED to launching motorized craft Nov 1-Jun 30 (waterfowl sanctuary), but loading/unloading non-motorized craft (canoes, kayaks, rafts) is allowed year-round, though you may have to carry boats to/from the parking lot. Monument is open sunrise to sunset; the launch is open 2 h before sunrise to 2 h after sunset for fishing entry (USFWS 2025 regulations brochure).
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~204), the ramp is on the east/south-east bank, left of the NHD centreline (~270 m; the reach is wide here). Confirmed on imagery.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Both endpoints are verified. Vernita Bridge comes from WDFW's field-confirmed ramp feature 25 plus the WDFW page and the WaterAccessSites layer. White Bluffs comes from USFWS's own facility asset point plus USFWS Hanford Reach pages. Banks come from NHDPlus HR. White Bluffs is closed to motorized launching Nov 1-Jun 30; non-motorized load/unload is allowed.
